title: Two paths to make brownfield OT data usable
summary: Explore how Belden and Microsoft use open standards like OPC UA and MQTT to help manufacturers connect and contextualize brownfield OT data for Azure IoT Operations.

## How to choose the right path


Belden connects factory assets and prepares their data: BHDO integrates PLC, SCADA and MES systems across more than 300 protocols, while LioN-X connects IO-Link sensors.


At the edge, Azure IoT Operations on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes discovers assets, brokers and transforms data, and then routes it through OPC UA, MQTT and other connectors.


In the Microsoft Azure cloud, centralized management and services such as Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Event Hubs and Azure Data Explorer, turn this operational data into governed pipelines, analytics and business insights.

## Why Belden and Microsoft work well together


- **Reliable networks for IT/OT convergence** : Belden provides a full network stack, including field cabling, IO-Link infrastructure, switches, routers and access points.


- **Security by design** : Belden strengthens industrial environments with a robust OT security portfolio (e.g., industrial firewalls and secure networking), while Microsoft brings decades of secure-by-design engineering through its security development lifecycle (SDL), delivering end-to-end defense-in-depth from the plant floor to the cloud.


- **Brownfield retrofitting** : Belden acquires, harmonizes and contextualizes industrial data at the edge. Transformed into a clear JSON structure, data points can be integrated through OPC UA or MQTT.


- **Unified data plane** : Microsoft brings the Arc-enabled Kubernetes data plane that offers modular and scalable data services, including native OPC UA integration and an edge MQTT broker.


- **Data integration** : Microsoft Azure IoT Operations connects IT and OT by providing a common edge runtime and structured data plane. It offers a governed path into Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Event Hubs and Azure Data Explorer.


## Start with the data source that matters most


The path to modernization looks different for every plant. Start with BHDO when controller data and protocol diversity are your primary challenges. Start with LioN-X when your priority is fast access to IO-Link sensor data and diagnostics.


In either case, open industrial standards provide the bridge into Azure IoT Operations and create a foundation for analytics and other data-driven applications.
